seo.title: What is static site generation?
seo.description: Static site generation builds pages into finished files ahead of time, so a request is answered by handing over a file that already exists.

definition: Static site generation builds pages into finished files ahead of time, so a request is answered by handing over a file that already exists.
answerBlock: Static site generation builds pages into finished files ahead of time, so a request is answered by handing over a file that already exists. It is the fastest way to serve a page and the cheapest to host. The cost is that a change to the content requires the affected pages to be rebuilt.

body.heading: When is a static page the right answer?
paragraphs: When the content is the same for everyone and does not change by the minute: service pages, articles, glossary entries, documentation. These can be built once and served from a cache near the visitor.

It is the wrong answer when a page depends on who is asking. Account pricing, stock levels, a dashboard or anything behind a login has to be rendered per request, because a cached copy would be someone else's data.
Modern frameworks mix the two, so most of a site can be static while the pages that must be live are rendered per request, and pages can be rebuilt on publish rather than on a deployment.

commercial.heading: Why does it matter commercially?
paragraphs: Static pages are hard to make slow, which protects the parts of the site that earn search traffic from whatever the rest of the platform is doing.
The operational question to ask a supplier is how long publishing takes: if a typo fix means a full rebuild and a deployment, editors will stop fixing typos.

example.heading: What does it look like in practice?
example.body: A glossary like this one is the textbook candidate: every entry is identical for every visitor, so the pages could be built once and served from a cache near the reader. We render them per request from our own API instead, because an edit made in the dashboard should be live at once rather than after a rebuild. That is the trade the technique asks you to make.

service.title: Next.js development
service.line: Fast, maintainable sites and applications on Next.js and React, including headless CMS builds, with a typed API and hosting in your name.

terms.definition: A headless CMS stores and edits content but does not render the pages that display it.
Server-side rendering means the server builds the finished HTML for a page and sends it, rather than sending an empty shell for the browser to fill in.
